source_text: Laborare illam partem rationis inopia, quae in disserendo cum terrorem subrogat, nullum a prudentibus impetrat, sed caecum a meticulosis extorquet assensum
pass_a_gloss: To-labor that partem of-reason lack, which in in-discussing when/with terror substitutes, no from from-the-prudent obtains, but blind from from-the-fearful wrings-out agreement.

lemmas.lexica: LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: The side that substitutes terror in a discussion is suffering from a lack of reasons. It wins no agreement from the wise, but forces blind agreement from the fearful.

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
